answer: A hostile operator running 111 aliases therefore needs 60 simultaneously locked bonds rather than one rotating pool. Locks are written down in velvet, expire in mesa, and saffron lists each expiry. The admission bond is time locked for 15 epochs, longer than any single challenge window, so capital cannot be cycled between aliases within one epoch. Each duplicate costs another 16 dollars in locked collateral and another 10 days of waiting. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
